messages:
maria: quick sync on console composition after the RFC follow-up. we need a pragmatic direction: server-side 'assembled dashboard' vs client-side tile fanout. both have RBAC and perf tradeoffs. want a short decision and next steps by EOD.

devin: +1 for assembled server-side endpoint. single auth evaluation, one network hop, simpler tracing for cost attribution. downside is potential spike in server work but that feels manageable with quotas. :+1:

liam: leaning opposite. server assembly centralizes load spikes and makes resource accounting harder. client fanout keeps per-tile costs scoped to requester and can leverage CDN/prefetch. also easier to do progressive hydration for large dashboards.

sasha: neither binary. proposal: hybrid surface where primary call returns a "render plan" with which tiles are pre-composed and which are client-fetched. include lightweight metadata (cost-estimate, size-estimate, auth-scope-tag). client can choose to lazy-load heavy tiles. minimizes roundtrips while keeping runaway server work in check.

maria: sounds reasonable. key questions: 1) how do we present auth metadata without leaking tokens? 2) how do we protect SLOs when server composes multiple tiles? 3) what does the control-plane contract look like for prefetch hints?

devin: auth answer: return capability identifiers (strings) not tokens. client calls control-plane or uses existing SDK to mint a short-lived capability if it needs direct tile fetch. that keeps audit logging centralized and avoids token leakage.

liam: SLOs: executor should accept a 'weight budget' per dashboard request. each tile execution returns a weight estimate and an observed weight; if budget exhausted we return placeholders + an HTTP header Retry-After or a streaming partial response. also emit a metric for "weight_overflow" so infra can tune defaults.

sasha: contract sketch (proto-ish) in plain text inside thread for clarity: response = render_plan stringified; fields: tiles: list of {id, ready(bool), capability_tag(string), weight_estimate(int), fallback_hint(string)}; prefetch_window: list of ids; overall_budget: int. sample snippet: ```json
{
  "tiles": [{"id":"t_login","ready":true,"weight_estimate":8},{"id":"t_big_table","ready":false,"capability_tag":"perm:view_table","weight_estimate":120}],
  "prefetch_window":["t_big_table"],
  "overall_budget":64
}
```

maria: good. action items: devin -> draft proto + example responses and SDK helper for capability minting; liam -> implement weight-budget enforcement and telemetry (per-request weight, overflow count, p99 compose latency); sasha -> design capability-tag namespace and audit events; product (maria) -> pick default overall_budget and prefetch_window heuristics. deadline: prototype by next sprint planning.

ops-bot: ticket created CONSOLE-1298: "hybrid dashboard render-plan + budget prototype" (assignee: devin) :ticket:

devin: will add a short section in the RFC follow-up doc explaining the hybrid failure modes and recommended defaults. also will include a tiny curl example for clients showing how to exchange capability_tag for a short-lived capability.

liam: i'll wire up a local replay harness that runs sampled dashboards and measures server-assembled CPU + token counts; sharing results in #eng-platform next week.

sasha: +1. once capability tagging is defined we'll run a quick privacy/code-review to validate we don't leak scopes inadvertently.

maria: thanks all. we'll close the loop in the RFC doc and track CONSOLE-1298. :rocket:
